claims.text: Increasing Cr and/or Al concentration promotes rapid formation of a protective oxide layer in high-entropy alloys.
The resulting protective oxide layer is adherent and fine-grained.
The protective oxide layer limits diffusion of oxygen and metal ions.
Limiting oxygen and metal-ion diffusion enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Elevated Cr and/or Al promotes a dense, continuous, fine-grained scale composed primarily of Cr2O3 and/or Al2O3.
Increasing reactive-element concentration raises the alloy surface's oxygen affinity.
Higher surface oxygen affinity triggers formation of a stable, adherent oxide layer.
The stable oxide layer significantly lowers oxygen and metal-ion diffusion rates and thereby retards further oxidation.
Relative to the baseline, the Cr/Al-enriched alloy will form a more uniform and adherent oxide scale.
Relative to the baseline, the oxide scale on the Cr/Al-enriched alloy will grow more slowly.
Relative to the baseline, the Cr/Al-enriched alloy will show lower oxidation-induced weight gain.
Microstructural analysis will show a finer-grained oxide morphology on the modified alloy.
The unmodified baseline alloy forms a less protective and potentially more porous oxide layer with a higher oxidation rate.
The proposed behavior applies approximately from 900 to 1100 degrees Celsius in air.
Water vapor, changes in gas composition, or temperatures outside 900–1100 degrees Celsius may produce different oxidation behavior.
Previous literature supports the qualitative effect of reactive-element concentration on protective oxide formation.
The quantitative reduction in oxidation rate and the reactive-element concentration required for optimal protection are uncertain.
